basis: A saddle horse a visitor may ride, tied in each year near where the walk begins. The horse is the driven current26 horse with its own coat; its saddle, bridle and stirrups are generated by renderers/web/js/saddlery.js from the tack below and fitted to the horse's own skin. The patterns are the common riding tack of each period as general horse history describes it (a plain hunting-pattern saddle on a blanket with a crupper in 1812, the English hunting saddle on a square cloth in 1835, the English flat saddle on a felt numnah in 1904); no source places these horses, saddles or owners here, and nothing here is an identified animal or saddle.

rider.why: The visitor in the saddle is drawn as a period figure of the year (an anonymous stand-in, never a named townsperson), posed by renderers/web/js/rider-pose.js: seat in the saddle, feet in the irons, hands on the reins.
rider.also_why: Figures the jaunts' scenes put on a horse besides the year's riders (jaunt-stage.js `mount`): the surgeon's mate Van Voorhis wears the First Infantry officer's coat (Wells wears the engagé's dress). tools/test_riding.mjs seats each of them; tools/compile_jaunts.py refuses a mount on any other.

1812.pattern: plain hunting-pattern saddle on a folded wool blanket, crupper and iron stirrups; plain snaffle bridle without a noseband

1835.pattern: English hunting saddle on a square saddle cloth, iron stirrups; snaffle bridle with a cavesson noseband

1904.pattern: English flat saddle on a shaped cream felt numnah, nickel stirrup irons; double bridle (bit and bridoon) with cavesson and browband

potawatomi.why: Kevin, 2026-11-17: "there would be horses at the native camps" and "People in long coats or blankets should be able to ride horses". The Potawatomi and Miami horsemen of the lakes rode on a low pad saddle of hide stuffed with hair, or a wooden-framed saddle covered in rawhide, over a trade blanket, with wooden stirrups; how any one horse was rigged is not recorded (L-camp-horses-3560).

set.pattern: low pad saddle of hide over a red stroud trade blanket, rawhide girth and crupper, wooden stirrups; a plain rawhide bridle

sidesaddle_1835.why: Kevin, 2026-11-17, on a card ("How should your person ride when you choose a woman?"): "Astride in 1812, sidesaddle later". A woman of the town in 1835 or 1904 rode aside, both legs on the near side. The saddle is a reconstructed period pattern, not a particular surviving saddle (L-sidesaddle-3644). Drawn with the fixed head alone, the pommel the right leg lies round: the leaping head (the pommel over the left thigh) was only coming into use in the 1830s and is left out.

set.pattern: side saddle with a flat seat and a fixed head on the near side, one iron stirrup on the near side, on the year's square saddle cloth; the year's snaffle bridle

sidesaddle_1904.why: Kevin, 2026-11-17, on a card ("How should your person ride when you choose a woman?"): "Astride in 1812, sidesaddle later". A woman of the town in 1835 or 1904 rode aside, both legs on the near side. The saddle is a reconstructed period pattern, not a particular surviving saddle (L-sidesaddle-3644). A 1904 side saddle had a leaping head as well, curving down over the left thigh; it lies under her skirt and is not drawn.

set.pattern: side saddle with a flat seat and its heads on the near side (the fixed head drawn; the leaping head lies under the skirt), one nickel stirrup on the near side, on the year's felt numnah; the year's double bridle

side_saddle.why: Kevin, 2026-11-17, on a card ("How should your person ride when you choose a woman?"): "Astride in 1812, sidesaddle later". A woman of the town in 1835 or 1904 rode aside, both legs on the near side. The saddle is a reconstructed period pattern, not a particular surviving saddle (L-sidesaddle-3644).

fit.basis: Metres in the horse root frame. A rider sits his seat bones in the saddle's deepest point (the pelvis joint ~9 cm above the seat leather); the iron hangs a leather's length under its bar and is pushed out round the barrel by the rider's leg; the ball of the foot on the tread with the heel down puts the ankle joint above and behind the iron; the hands carried a little above and ahead of the withers, a hand's breadth apart.
fit.bodies_basis: T-3644: a woman's body (wider at the hip than the men's this fit was made on) sits a little deeper, the knee carried more out than forward, and the thigh rolled in from the hip so its flat lies to the saddle, as a rider is taught; with the men's lines her inner thigh stood in the barrel (7.9 cm on woman_working_1812). Measured by tools/test_riding.mjs: every one of these bodies clear of the horse at walk, trot, canter and gallop, rising at the trot and moving with the horse (riderLife).

side.basis: T-3644: aside, on a side saddle. The seat square to the front; the right thigh forward round the fixed head, the knee lifted to it and the lower leg down the near shoulder; the left leg under it, its foot in the one, near, iron on a shorter leather. Measured by tools/test_riding.mjs: every woman's body of 1835 and 1904 clear of the horse at every pace, her legs under the habit (rider-drape.js), the fixed head clear of her leg.
